<ExternalIntegrationHeader integration={{"name":"NetAlertX","description":"Who is on your network: presence of each device, and an alert when an unknown one connects.","owner":"guim31","owner_avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/33096540?v=4","repo_url":"https://github.com/guim31/gladys-netalertx","cover_url":"https://integration-store-storage.gladysassistant.com/covers/guim31--gladys-netalertx.png","type":"device","version":"1.0.0","gladys_version":">=5.1.0","stars":0,"pushed_at":"2026-10-22T07:13:32Z"}} />

Know who is on your network from Gladys. [NetAlertX](https://github.com/netalertx/NetAlertX)
(formerly Pi.Alert) scans your network and keeps the list of every device it has seen. This
integration brings that list into Gladys: the presence of the phones, computers and other devices
you choose to follow, counters for the whole network, and above all a **scene trigger when an
unknown device connects**.

Typical uses: be notified on your phone when a device nobody knows joins the Wi-Fi, mark someone
at home when their phone is on the network, get an alert when the NAS or a camera drops off the
network, see at a glance on the dashboard which new devices still need to be acknowledged.

> **Tested against a real NetAlertX (26.10.0, in Docker), not yet on a real home installation:
> feedback welcome.** The integration was checked against the real NetAlertX API (devices joining,
> leaving, a new device, "mark as known"), but not yet with a real Gladys and a real home network.
> Tell us on the Gladys forum how it behaves for you.

## What you get

- A **NetAlertX network** device, the summary of the whole network:

  | Feature             | Type in Gladys    | Shows                                                        |
  | ------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
  | **Devices online**  | counter (integer) | devices present at the last NetAlertX scan                   |
  | **Devices offline** | counter (integer) | devices missing from the last scan                           |
  | **New devices**     | counter (integer) | devices NetAlertX flags as new (not acknowledged yet)        |
  | **Down alerts**     | counter (integer) | offline devices whose **Alert Down** is enabled in NetAlertX |

- **One device per network device you choose to follow** (every device of NetAlertX is proposed
  in the Discover tab, archived ones excepted):

  | Feature        | Type in Gladys           | Shows                                                      |
  | -------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
  | **Presence**   | presence sensor (yes/no) | "Presence detected" while NetAlertX sees it on the network |
  | **IP address** | text                     | its last IP address                                        |
  | **Last seen**  | text                     | the last time NetAlertX saw it, in the time zone of Gladys |

- A dashboard widget, **Network watch**: devices online, new devices and devices down, with a
  **Known** button for the new ones.
- Four scene triggers (**A new device joins the network**, **A device leaves the network**, **A
  device is back on the network**, **A watched device is down**) and one scene action, **Mark a
  device as known (NetAlertX)**.

## Requirements

- Gladys Assistant **5.1.0** or later (widgets, scene triggers and actions).
- A running **NetAlertX** that Gladys can reach on the local network. The integration reads its
  API (the "GraphQL" backend, port **20212** by default, setting `GRAPHQL_PORT`), not the web
  interface (port 20211). NetAlertX 26.x was tested; any version with the API token and the
  GraphQL API (2024 and later) should work.
- The **API token** of NetAlertX: in its web interface, **Settings → General → API token**
  (setting `API_TOKEN`, it starts with `t_`).
- Nothing else: no cloud, no account. NetAlertX does the scanning, the integration only reads its
  results.

## Configuration

### Settings

1. Install the integration (**Integrations → Install from GitHub**, address
   `https://github.com/guim31/gladys-netalertx`), then open its **Configuration** tab.
2. **API address**: the IP address or name of the NetAlertX server, e.g. `192.168.1.10`. Without a
   port, `20212` is used; add `:port` if you changed `GRAPHQL_PORT`, and use `https://` if the API
   sits behind a reverse proxy.
3. **API token**: paste the `API_TOKEN` of NetAlertX.
4. **Read interval**: how often the integration reads the device list (1 minute by default).
   NetAlertX itself scans every 5 minutes by default (`ARPSCAN_RUN_SCHD`): reading more often only
   catches a scan sooner.
5. **Language of the names**: language of the names given to new devices and their features, of
   the messages and of the dates (French by default).
6. Save. The connection status turns green, and the devices appear in the **Discover** tab.

### Configuration actions

- **Test the connection**: reads NetAlertX once and says how many devices it knows, how many are
  online and how many are new.
- **Mark every new device as known**: right after installing NetAlertX, every device is "new".
  This clears the flag on all of them at once, so only the devices that join later count as new
  (in the counter, the widget and the trigger).

### Choosing the devices

In the **Discover** tab, add the **NetAlertX network** device for the counters, and the devices
you want to follow one by one (phones, computers, servers, cameras…). The others stay in NetAlertX:
the triggers work for every device of NetAlertX, created in Gladys or not.

## Devices

- **Presence** follows the "present in the last scan" of NetAlertX: it changes at the scan that
  sees the device leave or come back, with no delay added by the integration. While the device is
  present, "present" is published again at every NetAlertX scan, so the **Check user presence**
  scene action of Gladys sees the device as recently seen (see the scene examples).
- **IP address** and **Last seen** are texts, updated when they change. The date comes from
  NetAlertX and is shown in the time zone of Gladys.
- The names are the ones NetAlertX shows (set them in NetAlertX before adding the device: the name
  is frozen at creation in Gladys). A device without a name shows its vendor and the end of its
  MAC address, or its MAC address.
- The four counters of **NetAlertX network** are kept in history: a chart shows how many devices
  were online over the day.

## Dashboard widget

**Network watch** shows three tiles (devices online, new devices, devices down), then the list of
the new devices (with their IP address, or "offline") and of the devices down, ten rows at most.
Each of the first four new devices gets a **Known** button, which marks it as known in NetAlertX.
When there is nothing to report, a short line says so.

## Scene triggers

| Trigger                             | Fires when                                                         | Filter              | Information passed on                    |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| **A new device joins the network**  | NetAlertX sees a device for the first time, flagged new            | none                | name, MAC address, vendor, IP address    |
| **A device leaves the network**     | a device seen at the previous scan is missing from the last one    | device (empty: any) | name, MAC address, IP address            |
| **A device is back on the network** | a device missing from the previous scan is seen again              | device (empty: any) | name, MAC address, IP address            |
| **A watched device is down**        | a device whose **Alert Down** is enabled in NetAlertX goes offline | device (empty: any) | name, MAC address, IP address, last seen |

The very first read after the installation only records the network: no trigger fires for the
devices already there. The integration remembers the last list it read (under `/data`), so a
restart neither announces every device again nor misses what changed while it was stopped. At most 20 events are sent per read, the next ones at the following reads; an event Gladys could not take (while it restarts) is sent again at the next read.

## Scene actions

- **Mark a device as known (NetAlertX)**: clears the "new" flag of a device in NetAlertX, as
  unticking **New Device** on its device page does. The **MAC address** field accepts scene variables: after the **A new
  device joins the network** trigger, insert its **MAC address**. It returns **Done (1 = yes)**;
  on an unknown device or NetAlertX unreachable, the action fails and the scene continues.

## Scene examples

- **Unknown device on the Wi-Fi**: trigger **A new device joins the network** → action **Send a
  message**: "New device on the network: \{name\} (\{vendor\}, \{ip\})". Add **Mark a device as known**
  with the MAC address at the end if you only want to be told once per device (it is otherwise
  told once anyway: the trigger only fires at its first appearance).
- **Someone is home**: trigger "a device changes state" on the **Presence** of their phone (equal
  to 1) → action **User seen at home**. A second scene, run every 10 minutes, does **Check user
  presence** with their phone and 15 minutes: Gladys marks them away once NetAlertX no longer
  sees it.
- **The NAS is down**: enable **Alert Down** on the NAS in NetAlertX, then trigger **A watched
  device is down** (device: the NAS) → send a message "The NAS left the network (last seen
  \{last seen\})".

## Troubleshooting

- **"NetAlertX refused the API token"**: copy the token again from **Settings → General → API
  token**. If you generate a new token in NetAlertX, update it here.
- **"This address does not answer like the NetAlertX API"**: the address points to the web
  interface (20211) or to another service. Use the API port, 20212 by default (`GRAPHQL_PORT`).
- **"NetAlertX does not answer"**: check that Gladys can reach the NetAlertX server and its port
  (firewall, Docker port published). With NetAlertX in Docker on the host network, the API listens
  on the host address.
- **A phone shows offline while at home**: phones asleep on Wi-Fi do not always answer the ARP
  scan, and recent phones use a private (random) MAC address per network. Turn the private
  address off for your home Wi-Fi, and see the "sleeping devices" settings of NetAlertX.
- **Every device is "new"**: that is how NetAlertX starts. Run **Mark every new device as known**
  once.
- **Logs**: the integration only writes the important events (NetAlertX lost and back, devices
  leaving, coming back, new devices). Set `LOG_LEVEL=debug` on the container to see every read.

## Limits

- The integration reads NetAlertX; it does not scan anything itself. Presence is only as fresh as
  the NetAlertX scans (every 5 minutes by default).
- **Last seen** assumes the dates of NetAlertX are in UTC, as in NetAlertX 26.x. Older versions
  stored local time: the hour may then be shifted.
- A device with "Alert Down" that NetAlertX lets sleep ("Can sleep") still fires **A watched
  device is down** when it drops off: the integration does not read the sleep window.
- Up to 500 devices are proposed in the Discover tab. Archived devices are ignored.
- The device filter of the triggers lists the devices created in Gladys; leave it empty to react
  to any device of NetAlertX.
- Not affiliated with NetAlertX.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings NetAlertX asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your NetAlertX | `section` | No | NetAlertX scans your network and keeps the list of its devices. In NetAlertX, copy the API token from Settings → General (API token). The integration reads the API, on port 20212 by default (GRAPHQL_PORT), not the web interface on 20211. |
| API address | `string` | Yes | IP address or name of the NetAlertX server, with :port if the API is not on 20212, and https:\/\/ behind a reverse proxy. |
| API token | `secret` | Yes | The API_TOKEN setting of NetAlertX (starts with t_). |
| Read interval | `select` | No | How often the device list of NetAlertX is read. NetAlertX itself scans every 5 minutes by default. |
| Language of the names | `select` | No | Names given to new devices and their features (Presence, IP address…), and language of the messages and dates. |

## How to install NetAlertX in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: NetAlertX appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/guim31/gladys-netalertx:1.0.0`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/guim31/gladys-netalertx](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-netalertx).

NetAlertX requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

NetAlertX is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [guim31](https://github.com/guim31), not by the Gladys core team.
